stories.headline: Starmer fights to survive Labour leadership crisis after disastrous local elections
stories.summary: Following Labour's loss of nearly 1,500 council seats in the May 7 local elections, Prime Minister Keir Starmer is fighting to retain his leadership amid calls to resign from Labour MPs, the resignation of Health Secretary Wes Streeting, and positioning by potential challengers including Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham and former Deputy PM Angela Rayner. Starmer has refused to set a timetable for departure, with Deputy PM David Lammy defending him publicly, while Burnham seeks a return to Parliament via the Makerfield by-election as a vehicle for a leadership challenge.

stories.headline: Reeves announces £1.8bn cost-of-living package including VAT cuts, fuel duty freeze, and food tariff reductions
stories.summary: Chancellor Rachel Reeves unveiled a 'Great British Summer Savings' scheme including a temporary VAT cut from 20% to 5% on family attractions, a freeze on fuel duty (cancelling a planned 5p rise), import tariff cuts on over 100 food products, and a new oil company tax loophole closure. The package was met with criticism as insufficient by the SNP and public readers, with health experts raising obesity concerns over food price cuts, while Reeves simultaneously backed away from a price cap on supermarket essentials after backlash from banks and retailers. UK borrowing hit its highest since COVID in April.

stories.headline: NATO allies alarmed by US troop withdrawal and force posture changes in Europe
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it would shrink the pool of military forces available to NATO in a crisis, and withdrew a 4,000-strong armoured brigade from Germany, causing confusion after Trump then announced an additional 5,000 troops for Poland. NATO foreign ministers met in Helsingborg, Sweden, where Secretary of State Rubio tried to reassure allies while pressing European nations to spend more on defence. European allies began quietly planning alternative defence structures in case of further US disengagement.

stories.headline: Bank of England and FCA unveil shared vision for tokenisation and 24/7 settlement in UK financial markets
stories.summary: The Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority launched a joint consultation on tokenisation of wholesale financial markets and announced plans to extend RTGS/CHAPS settlement hours to include Sundays, as part of a broader push towards near-24/7 payments. Separately, the BoE governor demanded Anthropic brief global regulators on its new AI model, and the Bank is revising proposed stablecoin holding limits following crypto industry pushback.

stories.headline: Nigel Farage's undisclosed £5 million gift investigated as he claims Russian hackers leaked the story
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage is under investigation by the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner over a £5 million gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, which Farage claims he did not need to declare as it pre-dated his return to Parliament. Farage further claimed his phone was hacked by Russian state actors who then leaked the story to media, a claim defended by Reform MP Robert Jenrick. A separate County Court judgment for an unpaid debt of approximately £9,400 from 2024 was also revealed.

stories.headline: Bank of England holds rates with Iran war complicating inflation outlook
stories.summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey and MPC members signalled that interest rate cuts — which had previously been anticipated — have effectively been 'taken off the table' due to inflation risks from the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz closure. The IMF urged the BoE not to hike, while MPC dove Alan Taylor argued rates remain far too restrictive for a weakening economy. Weakening jobs data and softer April inflation provided some relief to rate-hike expectations.

stories.headline: King Charles Northern Ireland visit: community engagements, seagull incident, radio station false death announcement
stories.summary: King Charles and Queen Camilla made a surprise, unannounced visit to Northern Ireland for security reasons, attending events in Belfast including a celebration of Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann, and community engagements in Newcastle, Co. Down. A seagull defecated on the King during the visit. Separately, Radio Caroline accidentally triggered its 'death of a monarch' protocol during the trip, broadcasting a false announcement of Charles's death for approximately 15 minutes before issuing an apology.

stories.headline: Police investigation into Prince Andrew expected to be lengthy and complex
stories.summary: Thames Valley Police confirmed that their investigation into Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor — arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office related to his Epstein connections — will be 'long and complex.' King Charles, who stripped Andrew of his titles last October, said he was 'deeply concerned.' Police are also separately investigating allegations that Andrew behaved inappropriately towards a woman at Royal Ascot in 2002.

stories.headline: Starmer welcomes progress in US-Iran talks and calls for unrestricted Strait of Hormuz access

Starmer stressed that any agreement must ensure 'unconditional and unrestricted' access to the Strait of Hormuz for shipping, which has been a key driver of UK energy price pressures.

stories.headline: Russian GPS jamming of RAF jet carrying Defence Secretary Healey on return from Estonia
stories.summary: A suspected Russian electronic attack jammed the GPS of an RAF aircraft carrying Defence Secretary John Healey as he returned from visiting British troops stationed in Estonia, forcing pilots to use alternative navigation for the entire three-hour flight. Healey condemned the action as 'unacceptable,' describing it as the most dangerous Russian action since 2022. It is unknown whether Healey was personally targeted.
